evidence.estrutura: Michelle Obama's public initiatives worked through federal programs, local schools, nonprofits and private partners. This supports pragmatic multilevel governance rather than a strong centralization or federalism doctrine.
evidence.representacao: Her public speeches and civic work consistently encourage participation, education, voting and inclusion, supporting representative democratic norms even though she has not held elected office.
evidence.poder: Her agenda emphasizes opportunity, education and community support rather than coercive state authority. The reviewed official sources do not establish a strong security-versus-liberty doctrine; use a moderately liberal position.
evidence.imigracao: Her initiatives are inclusive and multicultural, but the reviewed official sources do not establish a detailed immigration or border policy. Keep moderate-to-inclusive.
evidence.diplomacia: Let Girls Learn and her international advocacy for girls' education relied on international partnerships, cultural diplomacy and development cooperation, supporting a diplomatic rather than militarist orientation.
evidence.intervencao: She has not articulated a detailed military-intervention doctrine. Her international public work is education- and development-based, supporting restraint.
evidence.economia: Her programs emphasize education, health, employment opportunity and public-private partnerships within a market economy. This supports a center-left mixed economy rather than state ownership or laissez-faire extremes.
evidence.controle: She accepts public health and education interventions while relying extensively on voluntary, nonprofit and private-sector cooperation. This supports moderate regulation and public coordination.
evidence.comercio: No reliable free-trade versus protectionism doctrine is established by her First Lady initiatives. Keep moderate.
evidence.religiao: Her public service operates within a secular constitutional framework, though she has a Christian personal background. No support exists for religious government.
evidence.moral: Her advocacy for girls' education, racial inclusion, healthy families and equal opportunity supports socially liberal and egalitarian values, though her public role was not defined by radical cultural-policy advocacy.
evidence.tecnologia: Her education and youth initiatives use modern media and evidence-based public-health tools but do not define a broad technology ideology. Use a moderate pro-modernization position.
